steps.label: The two varieties
lines: Two semi-dwarf rice varieties developed in India:
steps.why: Both were bred in India during the green revolution, which is why they are the named pair for this question.
common_mistakes: Naming Sonalika and Kalyan Sona. Those are WHEAT varieties.
Naming basmati. Basmati is the patent case, not a semi-dwarf variety.
steps.memory_tip: Jaya and Ratna for rice; Sonalika and Kalyan Sona for wheat.

steps.label: Why semi-dwarf
steps.margin_note: Name lodging and explain the link to fertiliser. Six lines.

lines.text: A short stem can carry a heavy head of grain

lines: A semi-dwarf plant has a SHORT, STRONG stem.
So it can carry a heavy head of grain without
That is what lets heavy fertiliser use turn into
extra yield instead of a flattened field.
steps.why: A tall plant given heavy fertiliser grows a head too heavy for its stem and falls over, so shortening the stem is what made high fertiliser use possible.
common_mistakes: Saying semi-dwarf means low yielding. It is HIGH yielding, precisely because it does not lodge.
Giving no reason. The reason is the second mark.
steps.memory_tip: Short stem, heavy head, no falling over.
